'''Louis Tyrone Williams''' (born October 27, 1986) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was drafted [[NBA high school draftees|directly out of high school]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] with the 45th overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]]. He is a 3-time [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]], a record he shares with [[Jamal Crawford]]. As of March 2019, he is the NBA's career leader in points off the bench,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/lou-williams-curry-bench-scoring|title=Williams passes Dell Curry for most bench points in NBA history|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=December 22, 2020}}</ref> and has played the most career games off the bench, surpassing [[Dell Curry]]'s record in February 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lou Williams Has The Most Games Played Off The Bench With 985|url=https://fadeawayworld.net/nba-media/lou-williams-has-the-most-games-played-off-the-bench-with-985|access-date=February 18, 2022|website=Fadeaway World|date=February 17, 2022 }}</ref>

Williams spent seven seasons with Philadelphia before signing with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in 2012, playing two seasons there before being traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the 2014 offseason. He spent a season with the Raptors and then signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] from 2015 until the middle of the [[2016–17 NBA season]], when he was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]]. After finishing the season with the Rockets, he was then traded in the 2017 offseason to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. Williams was dealt back to the Hawks in 2021.

==High school career==
Williams was born in [[Memphis, Tennessee]] and moved to [[Atlanta]] in his teens.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120308060658/http://louwilliamsfoundation.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=112&Itemid=132 About Us – The Lou Williams Foundation]</ref> Williams played at Snellville's [[South Gwinnett High School]] under Roger Fleetwood, where he was a four-time All-State selection and was named Georgia's "Mr. Basketball" as a senior. As a junior, Williams led South Gwinnett to the 5A Georgia State Championship. At the end of his senior year, Williams was named the [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] and a [[McDonald's All-American Team|McDonald's All-American]] as well as a first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]]. Lou Williams also participated in the [[Nike Hoop Summit]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]].

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Williams was listed as the No. 1 shooting guard and the No. 3 player in the nation overall in 2005.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Louis-Williams-18539 Louis Williams – Yahoo! Sports]</ref>

Williams, and high school teammate [[Mike Mercer (basketball)|Mike Mercer]], committed to play at the [[University of Georgia]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2052751|title=Jack, prep star Williams to announce draft plans|date=May 4, 2005|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> for then-coach [[Dennis Felton]], but Williams ended up declaring for the [[2005 NBA draft]] instead.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2053466|title=Naismith prep POY Williams declares for draft|date=May 5, 2005|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Williams finished his career as the all-time leading scorer in Georgia high school basketball history.

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia 76ers (2005–2012)===
Williams was picked in the 2nd round of the draft and 45th overall by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He played  over thirty games in his rookie season, averaging 1.9 points and 0.3 assists.

The next season, Williams was sent to play for the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] on November 28, 2006.<ref>Hollis, John & Haddocks, Robert (2006): ''[http://www.ajc.com/metro/content/metro/gwinnett/stories/2006/11/28/1129gwxlouis.html Louis Williams demoted by 76ers]'', ''[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]'' 11/28/06</ref> After a good showing in the D-League,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/louis_williams/game_by_game_stats.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104143117/http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/louis_williams/game_by_game_stats.html|title=Game-by-game NBADL statistics|website=[[NBA.com]] |archive-date=November 4, 2012}}</ref> and trade rumors surrounding 76ers' starting point guard [[Allen Iverson]],<ref>Jasner, Phil (2006): ''[http://www.philly.com/mld/dailynews/sports/16201100.htm A.I. will soon be history]'', ''[[Philadelphia Daily News]]'' 12/09/06</ref> Williams was recalled back to the 76ers' roster on December 8, 2006.

During the 2007–08 season, Williams averaged 11.3 ppg, 3.2 apg and 2.0 rpg. At the end of that season, Williams became a restricted free agent and signed a five-year deal worth $25 million to remain with Philadelphia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3519199|title=Restricted free agent Williams re-signs with 76ers|date=August 4, 2008|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In game 4 of the first round of the 2011 Eastern Conference Playoffs, Williams hit a go-ahead [[three-pointer]] to give the 76ers a win against the [[Miami Heat]], 86–82.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310424020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820065408/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310424020|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 20, 2016|title=Heat vs. 76ers – Game Recap – April 24, 2011 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> However, the Sixers ended up losing the series in five games.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310427014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820065026/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310427014|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 20, 2016|title=76ers vs. Heat – Game Recap – April 27, 2011 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>
[[File:Louis Williams 76ers vs Wizards.jpg|thumb|Williams with the 76ers in 2010]]
For the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]], Williams led the 76ers in scoring with 14.9 points per game, despite not starting a single game.<ref name=sixthman2012>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7916436/oklahoma-city-thunder-james-harden-wins-nba-sixth-man-year-award|title=Thunder's Harden wins Sixth Man of the Year|date=May 10, 2012|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He was the runner-up finisher for the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]].<ref name=sixthman2012/>

===Atlanta Hawks (2012–2014)===
On July 12, 2012, Williams signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-free-agent-guard-lou-williams-contract | title=HAWKS SIGN FREE AGENT GUARD LOU WILLIAMS TO A CONTRACT | work=NBA.com | date=July 12, 2012 | access-date=July 15, 2012}}</ref> On January 18, 2013, against the [[Brooklyn Nets]], Williams landed awkwardly on his right knee and had to leave the game on a wheelchair. It was later revealed that he tore his [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ACL]] and would miss the rest of the season.

Williams missed the first few games of the 2013–14 season while recovering from his knee injury. He made his debut on November 20, 2013, scoring 6 points off the bench. On December 14, 2013, Williams scored a season high of 27 points. He finished the season with averages of 10.4 points, 3.5 assists, and 2.1 rebounds.

===Toronto Raptors (2014–2015)===
On June 30, 2014, Williams was traded, along with the draft rights to [[Lucas Nogueira]], to the Toronto Raptors in exchange for [[John Salmons]] and a 2015 second round pick.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/trade_063014|title=Raptors Acquire Williams, Nogueira From Atlanta|website=Toronto Raptors}}</ref> On November 22, 2014, he scored a then career-high 36 points in the Raptors' 110–93 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141122/TORCLE/gameinfo.html|title=Williams, Raptors beat struggling Cavs, 110–93|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> On April 20, 2015, Williams was named the 2015 [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]], becoming the first member of the Toronto Raptors to ever win the award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/20/lou-williams-wins-2014-14-kia-sixth-man-award/|title=Raptors' Lou Williams wins 2014–15 Kia NBA Sixth Man Award|work=NBA.com|date=April 20, 2015|access-date=April 20, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Devine|first=Dan|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/raptors--lou-williams-wins-2014-15-nba-sixth-man-of-the-year-award-181007316.html|title=Raptors' Lou Williams wins 2014–15 NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award|work=Yahoo.com|date=April 20, 2015|access-date=April 20, 2015}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2015–2017)===
On July 9, 2015, Williams signed a three-year, $21 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/150708_louWilliams|title=Lakers Sign Lou Williams|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2015|access-date=July 9, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/13202908/los-angeles-lakers-lou-williams-agree-contract|title=Sources: Lakers reach deal with Sixth Man of the Year Lou Williams|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=ESPN news services|date=July 6, 2015|access-date=July 6, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Lakers in the season opener against the Minnesota Timberwolves on October 28, 2015, scoring 21 points off the bench in a 112–111 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Wolves edge Lakers 112–111 in first game since Flip's death|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 29, 2015}}</ref> On January 3, 2016, he scored a then season-high 30 points in a 97–77 win over the Phoenix Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160103/PHXLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Williams scores 30, Lakers beat Suns 97–77 without Kobe|work=NBA.com|date=January 3, 2016|access-date=January 3, 2016}}</ref> Five days later, he scored 23 of his then career-high 44 points in the fourth quarter of the Lakers' 117–113 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160108/OKCLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Westbrook, Thunder hold off Lakers 117–113 despite Lou's 44|work=NBA.com|date=January 8, 2016|access-date=January 9, 2016}}</ref>

On December 3, 2016, Williams scored a season-high 40 points off the bench in a 103–100 loss to the Memphis Grizzlies. Williams's 40 points were the most ever scored by an opponent's reserve against Memphis, and he became the first player to score 40 off the bench since [[Jordan Crawford]] in April 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899737|title=Daniels scores career-best 31 to lead Grizzlies past Lakers|work=ESPN.com|date=December 3, 2016|access-date=December 4, 2016}}</ref> Two days later, he had 38 points, six rebounds and seven assists in a 107–101 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]], putting together the first back-to-back 30-point games of his 12-year NBA career. He also became the first Lakers player to score at least 38 points in successive games since [[Kobe Bryant]] in March 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899755|title=Jazz hold off Lakers' rally to win without Snyder, 107–101|work=ESPN.com|date=December 5, 2016|access-date=December 6, 2016}}</ref> Over four games between December 3 and 9, Williams scored 137 points—the biggest four-game scoring performance by a reserve since the NBA began keeping track of starts in 1970.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899786|title=Eric Bledsoe scores 30, Suns hold off Lakers 119–115|work=ESPN.com|date=December 9, 2016|access-date=December 10, 2016}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2017)===
On February 23, 2017, Williams was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Corey Brewer]] and a 2017 first-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-acquire-lou-williams|title=Rockets Acquire Lou Williams|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}}</ref> He made his debut for the Rockets that night, scoring 27 points with seven three-pointers off the bench in a 129–99 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900258|title=Rockets rout Pelicans, 129–99, in Cousins' New Orleans debut|work=ESPN.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017}}</ref> On March 15, 2017, he scored 30 points in a 139–100 win over the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900405|title=Williams, Harden send Rockets to 139–100 win over Lakers|work=ESPN.com|date=March 15, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2017}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2017–2021)===

====2017–18 season====
On June 28, 2017, the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] acquired Williams, [[Patrick Beverley]], [[Sam Dekker]], [[Montrezl Harrell]], [[Darrun Hilliard]], [[DeAndre Liggins]], [[Kyle Wiltjer]], and a 2018 first-round pick from the Houston Rockets in exchange for [[Chris Paul]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-la-clippers-acquire-seven-players-and-draft-pick-including-beverley-dekker-harrell-and|title=Press Release: L.A. Clippers Acquire Seven Players and Draft Pick, Including Beverley, Dekker, Harrell and Williams|work=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2017|access-date=June 28, 2017}}</ref> On November 27, 2017, Williams scored a season-high 42 points in a 120–115 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975048|title=Clippers hang on to beat Lakers 120–115 for 3rd win in row|work=ESPN.com|date=November 27, 2017|access-date=November 28, 2017}}</ref> On December 9, 2017, he hit a go-ahead pull-up 3-pointer with 1.2 seconds remaining, lifting the Clippers to a 113–112 victory over the [[Washington Wizards]]. He finished with 35 points to lead a dominant bench effort for the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975126|title=Williams' 3-pointer gives Clippers 113–112 win over Wizards|work=ESPN.com|date=December 9, 2017|access-date=December 10, 2017}}</ref> On December 31, 2017, he scored 40 points off the bench in a 106–98 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975288|title=Lou Williams scores 40 points, Clippers hold off Hornets|work=ESPN.com|date=December 31, 2017|access-date=December 31, 2017}}</ref> Williams was subsequently named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, December 25 through Sunday, December 31.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-lou-williams-named-western-conference-player-week|title=Press Release: Lou Williams Named Western Conference Player of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=January 2, 2018|access-date=January 3, 2018}}</ref> On January 10, 2018, he scored 27 of his career-high 50 points in the third quarter of the Clippers' 125–106 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He shot 16 for 27 with a career-best eight 3-pointers and made all 10 of his free throws.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975359|title=Lou Williams scores career-high 50, Clippers beat Warriors|work=ESPN.com|date=January 10, 2018|access-date=January 10, 2018}}</ref> It was the highest scoring effort by any Clipper in a single game since [[Charles Smith (basketball, born 1965)|Charles Smith]] tied a franchise record with 52 points in December 1990.<ref name=pow2>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-lou-williams-named-western-conference-player-week-0|title=Press Release: Lou Williams Named Western Conference Player of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=January 15, 2018|access-date=January 15, 2018}}</ref> Williams was subsequently named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, January 8 through Sunday, January 14.<ref name="pow2" /> On January 20, 2018, he recorded 31 points, a franchise-record 10 steals, and seven assists in a 125–113 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]]. He became the first player in league history to reach 30 points, 10 steals, and seven assists in a game since steals became a recorded stat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975427|title=Mitchell gets 23, Jazz end Clippers' streak with 125–113 win|work=ESPN.com|date=January 20, 2018|access-date=January 20, 2018}}</ref> On January 26, 2018, he had 40 points and matched his season high with 10 assists in the Clippers' 109–100 victory over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975464|title=Williams has 40 points,10 assists, Clippers beat Grizzlies|work=ESPN.com|date=January 26, 2018|access-date=January 26, 2018}}</ref> On February 7, 2018, he signed a multi-year contract extension with the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-la-clippers-sign-lou-williams-contract-extension|title=Press Release: L.A. Clippers Sign Lou Williams to Contract Extension|work=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2018|access-date=February 7, 2018}}</ref> On February 23, 2018, he had 35 points in 33 minutes, including a 23-point second quarter, in a 128–117 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975627|title=Williams, Clippers rout sinking Suns 128–117|work=ESPN.com|date=February 23, 2018|access-date=February 24, 2018}}</ref> Williams averaged career highs in points (22.6), assists (5.3), and minutes (32.8) during the 2017–18 season. His bench scoring led the NBA in his 13th season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975974|title=Hart's 30 lead Lakers past Clippers 115–100 to end season|work=ESPN.com|date=April 11, 2018|access-date=April 11, 2018}}</ref> He was subsequently named [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award|NBA Sixth Man of the Year]] for the second time in his career.<ref>{{cite web|last=Winfield|first=Kristian|url=https://www.sbnation.com/2018/6/25/17504590/lou-williams-wins-nba-sixth-man-of-the-year-clippers|title=Lou Williams wins NBA Sixth Man of the Year|work=sbnation.com|date=June 25, 2018|access-date=June 25, 2018}}</ref>

2019}}</ref> On March 17, he scored 25 points and hit a 28-foot 3-pointer from the top of the key at the buzzer to give the Clippers a 119–116 victory over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071722|title=Williams' 3-pointer lifts Clippers to 119–116 win over Nets|work=ESPN.com|date=March 17, 2019|access-date=March 18, 2019}}</ref>

On April 15, 2019, Williams had 36 points and 11 assists to help the Clippers overcome a 31-point deficit—the biggest comeback in NBA playoff history—and tie the first-round series at 1–1 against the Warriors with a 135–131 win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game?gameId=401126816|title=Clippers vs. Warriors – Game Summary – April 15, 2019 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=April 16, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/clippers-news-la-completes-the-biggest-comeback-in-nba-playoff-history/|title=BREAKING: Clippers Stun Warriors With Biggest Comeback In NBA Playoff History|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=April 16, 2019|website=ClutchPoints|language=en-US|access-date=April 16, 2019}}</ref> He became only the second bench player in NBA history with a 30-point, 10-assist performance in the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web|author=ESPN|url=https://twitter.com/espn/status/1118024226726981633|title=Sweet Lou!|work=Twitter|date=April 15, 2019|access-date=April 16, 2019}}</ref> In Game 5 of the series, he had 33 points and 10 assists in a 129–121 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401126822|title=Lou Williams, Clippers force Game 6 against champ Warriors|work=ESPN.com|date=April 24, 2019|access-date=April 25, 2019}}</ref> The Clippers went on to lose Game 6 to bow out of the playoffs. At the [[2019 NBA Awards|NBA's end-of-season awards night]], Williams was named the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award|NBA's Sixth Man of the Year]], joining [[Jamal Crawford]] as the only three-time winners of the award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/lou-williams-wins-2018-19-nba-kia-sixth-man-year-award|title=Lou Williams Wins The 2018–19 NBA KIA Sixth Man Of The Year Award|work=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2019|access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref>

====2019–20 season====
After violating the [[2020 NBA Bubble#Rules |rules]] of the [[2020 NBA Bubble |NBA Bubble]], Williams was required to sit out the first two seeding games of the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]] to fulfill his quarantine requirements.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2020/07/26/lou-williams-10-day-quarantine|title=Clippers' Lou Williams in 10-day quarantine after returning to Orlando|first=Shaun|last=Powell|website=NBA.com}}</ref> In the [[2020 NBA playoffs]], he struggled throughout the postseason, having averages of 12.8 points and 4.2 assists as the Clippers fell in seven games against the Denver Nuggets while surrendering a 3–1 lead in the Western Conference semi-finals.

====2020–21 season====
On February 14, 2021, Williams logged 30 points and 10 assists, both season-highs, in a 128–111 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Williams' 30 points leads Clippers in 128–111 rout of Cavs|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2021/02/15/williams-30-points-leads-clippers-in-128-111-rout-of-cavs.html|access-date=December 16, 2021|website=The Toronto Star|date=February 15, 2021 }}</ref>

===Return to Atlanta (2021–2022)===
On March 25, 2021, Williams, two second-round draft picks, and cash considerations were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Rajon Rondo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-veteran-lou-williams-la-clippers|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Veteran Lou Williams From LA Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021}}</ref> With his hometown team, Williams reached the Conference Finals for the first time in his career and played a career high 18 playoff games with his Atlanta Hawks. On August 6, 2021, he re-signed with the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Re-Sign Lou Williams|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-re-sign-lou-williams|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 6, 2021|date=August 6, 2021}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On June 18, 2023, Williams announced his retirement after a 17-year career at the age of 36. By the time his career was over, Williams had scored 13,396 points off the bench, which stands as an NBA record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37873057/lou-williams-three-sixth-man-year-retires-nba|title=Lou Williams, three-time Sixth Man of the Year, retires from NBA|work=ESPN.com|date=June 18, 2023|access-date=June 18, 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Williams is the son of Willie Louis Williams and Janice Faulkner. He has two brothers, Taurus Stinnett and Willie Louis Williams II, and one sister, Shaun Haynes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/louis_williams/bio/|title=Louis Williams Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> Williams has three children. He is a close friend of [[Bow Wow (rapper)|Bow Wow]] and was seen socializing with him at his house on an episode of ''[[MTV Cribs]]''.<ref>{{YouTube|Um9cXnGlVDU}}</ref>

Williams has recorded several rap tracks and was featured on [[Meek Mill]]'s single "I Want It All".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://rapradar.com/2011/03/30/new-video-meek-mill-x-lou-williams-i-want-it-all/|title=New Video: Meek Mill x Lou Williams "I Want It All"|website=Rap Radar|date=March 30, 2011 }}</ref>

He runs an annual summer camp at South Gwinnett High School, his alma mater, for children ages 10–16. "This camp means a lot to me because I can give back to a community that has done so much for me", Williams said.

In December 2011, Williams claimed his NBA recognition saved him from an armed robbery attempt in the Philadelphia neighborhood of Manayunk. A gunman allegedly tried to rob Williams but stopped and said he was a fan of the player. After Williams and the gunman reached an understanding, Williams bought him food from [[McDonald's]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7391657/lou-williams-philadelphia-76ers-says-won-armed-robber|title=76ers' Williams says he won over armed robber|date=December 27, 2011|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In 2014, it was revealed that Williams was dating both Ashley Henderson and Rece Mitchell at the same time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/sports/2014/12/lou-williams-raptors-sg-two-girlfriends-jr-smith-impressed|title=Raptors Guard Lou Williams Allegedly Has Two Girlfriends, J.R. Smith Is Very Impressed|website=Complex}}</ref> As of 2018, his relationship with Henderson had ended.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/sports/2018/02/lou-williams-talks-about-breaking-up-1-of-his-2-girlfriends|title=Lou Williams Talks About Breaking Up With 1 of His 2 Girlfriends|website=Complex}}</ref>

He is the subject of a song by Canadian rapper [[Drake (rapper)|Drake]] called "6 Man" on Drake's mixtape ''[[If You're Reading This It's Too Late]]''. Drake referenced Williams' role as a [[sixth man]] for the Raptors, as well as his alleged two girlfriends. The song was released on February 12, 2015, the same season Williams won the Sixth Man of the Year Award. The song was played during Williams' trophy presentation during the Raptors [[2015 NBA Playoffs|playoff game]] against the [[Washington Wizards]], and he is featured in the song's music video: a promotion for [[OVO Sound|OVO]]'s Raptors themed Spring 2015 Apparel.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/sports/2015/03/lou-williams-stars-in-video-for-drakes-6-man|title=Lou Williams Stars in Video For Drake's OVO Raptors-Inspired Spring Line|website=Complex}}</ref>

In July 2020, while on an excused absence from the Orlando [[2020 NBA Bubble|NBA quarantine bubble]], Williams attended a funeral viewing for Paul G. Williams, the father of a family friend. After the viewing, Williams went to the [[Magic City (club)|Magic City]] [[Strip club|gentlemen's club]] for dinner. The controversy caused NBA investigators to question Williams and assess the length of his re-quarantining process. It also led to him receiving the nickname Lemon Pepper Lou.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29538441/nba-probes-clippers-lou-williams-actions-away-bubble|title=Clippers' Lou Williams investigated by NBA about actions while on leave|website=ESPN|date=July 25, 2020}}</ref>

After an interview on a podcast, Lou Williams gained the nickname "Lemon Pepper Lou" which originates from the type of seasonings preferred on chicken wings while visiting the aforementioned gentlemen's club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lemoncelli |first=Jenna |date=2022-07-25 |title=Lou Williams talks Magic City strip club story in NBA Bubble |url=https://nypost.com/2022/07/25/lou-williams-talks-magic-city-strip-club-story-in-nba-bubble/ |access-date=2025-02-06 |language=en-US}}</ref>
